items.author: Pushkal-Gupta
items.summary: Adds missing `validate_max_output_tokens` check to the Rust frontend `/v1/responses` route so it rejects oversized budgets with 400, matching Python behavior.
items.body:
## Overview

`/v1/responses` on the Rust frontend accepts a `max_output_tokens` larger than `max_model_len`. It clamps the budget, runs the request and returns 200 with `status: "incomplete"`. The Python frontend rejects the same request with a 400. Rust's chat and completions routes already reject it through `validate_max_output_tokens`, but the Responses route never calls that check. This PR adds the call.

items.title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] Keep dotted Kimi K2 tool names whole, like Python
items.author: Pushkal-Gupta
items.summary: Fixes Rust kimi_k2 tool parser to preserve dotted tool names in full instead of truncating to the last segment, matching Python behavior.
items.body:
## Overview

The Rust `kimi_k2` tool parser cuts a dotted tool name down to its last segment. Kimi K2 writes a call header as `functions.{name}:{index}`, so a tool named `get-weather.v2` comes out of the model as `functions.get-weather.v2:0`, and Rust returns the name `v2`. The client then gets a call to a tool it never defined. Python returns `get-weather.v2`. This PR makes Rust read the header the way Python does.

## Claims

- A dotted tool name (`get-weather.v2`, `github.create_issue`) now keeps every segment, streaming and non-streaming.
- The tool call ID is unchanged: it was already t

items.author: AkiYangDev

On Ascend 950, static DSpark verify replay can receive sequence lengths exclusively on device. The replay context then stores device tensors in its `*_seq_lens_cpu` fields. Mac M3 Pro, CPU-only. Parser-only reproduction against current `main` (no GPU / no weights).

Follow-up from #69243: a fenced markdown example of a Ripple tool call is still executed as a **real** tool call.

items.title: [Fix] watermark: Seed each request's watermark once and commit with a mask
items.author: hnyls2002
items.summary: A watermark keeps per-request state: Gumbel's recent tokens and watermarked contexts, SynthID's context, history ring and call count. That state should start once, from the request, and after that change only when one of the request's tokens is committed.
items.body:
Stacked on #53664.

## Summary

A watermark keeps per-request state: Gumbel's recent tokens and watermarked contexts, SynthID's context, history ring and call count. That state should start once, from the request, and after that change only when one of the request's tokens is committed. Before this PR, `ForwardBatch.init_new` built a seed payload for every extend batch and the sample stage reseeded every prefill row at every chunk. `Argmax::pick` can panic with a division by zero. It reads the in-flight load of every tied candidate to find the minimum, then reads the loads again to collect the candidates at that minimum. items.title: [Bugfix][Distributed] Add RowParallelLinear bias after the all-reduce
items.author: bantianyue
items.summary: Fixes XLA graph divergence in tensor-parallel RowParallelLinear by adding bias after all-reduce instead of fusing it into rank-0 GEMM only.
items.body:
## Overview

`RowParallelLinear.forward` and `RowParallelLinearWithLoRA.forward` fused the bias into the GEMM on rank 0 only, so backends that compile one graph per rank (vllm-torchtpu on XLA) get different graphs across ranks, which breaks the all-reduce. Both forwards now add the bias after the all-reduce when reducing across ranks.

Fixes #70000 (request 1 only; the LoRA layer-class registration hook in request 2 is out of scope here).

- `RowParallelLinear` and `RowParallelLinearWithLoRA` produce identical graphs on all ranks when `tp_size > 1`: the bias is added after the all

items.author: hnyls2002

The default beam shared-context attention kernel computes `slot * stride` in int32. items.author: BBuf
items.summary: MiniMax-H3-Image edits already reuse individual encoded reference tiles. Repeated references still perform tile lookup, blend and assembly before drawing a fresh latent from the posterior.
items.body:
## Motivation

MiniMax-H3-Image edits already reuse individual encoded reference tiles. Repeated references still perform tile lookup, blend and assembly before drawing a fresh latent from the posterior.

## Modifications

Cache the deterministic, assembled posterior moments of a single-frame reference in the existing conditioning cache. On a miss, the tile lookups still run and can reuse unchanged tiles. Each edit samples a fresh latent using its request generator. Distributed tile assembly continues to execute on every participating rank.

Baseline `075ccb8add6d69f5a1954fae1bce3920adc422ef`.

items.title: [Fix] [AMD] scheduler: Enable the WAR barrier by default on ROCm
items.author: ksmotiv8
items.summary: turns the overlap scheduler's write-after-read barrier on by default only when is true, and is False under HIP. So on ROCm the barrier is off unless is set.
items.body:
## Motivation

`is_war_barrier_enabled()` turns the overlap scheduler's write-after-read barrier on by default only when `is_cuda()` is true, and `is_cuda()` is False under HIP. So on ROCm the barrier is off unless `SGLANG_ENABLE_WAR_BARRIER=1` is set. The schedule stream can then free KV slots and rewrite `req_to_token` rows while a forward that was launched earlier still reads them. One case is a finished prefill's prompt going into the radix tree: its duplicate prefix slots are freed, its row is re-pointed at the tree's slots, and a new prefill writes the freed slots.

This supersedes #3825

items.title: [Fix] attention: Correct carried-state decay in Minimax lightning prefill
items.author: ruiling-smartbear
items.summary: With, fresh prefill produces incorrect outputs starting at zero-based token 256, and continuation prefill is incorrect from its first token when the incoming state is nonzero. Thanks to @dreaming-panda for the detailed report and reproducer.
items.body:
## Motivation

Fixes #53616.

With `linear_backend="minimax"`, fresh prefill produces incorrect outputs starting at zero-based token 256, and continuation prefill is incorrect from its first token when the incoming state is nonzero. Thanks to @dreaming-panda for the detailed report and reproducer.

## Modifications

Fixes #70420

TRITON_MLA allocated its decode LSE in the query dtype, so with a bf16 model the fp32 LSE computed by the stage-2 kernel was rounded on store. items.title: [Perf] Diffusion: Reuse decoded PNG references across edit requests
items.author: BBuf
items.summary: Caches decoded RGB PNGs by content digest in the conditioning cache to skip repeated Pillow decompression on reused image inputs during diffusion editing.
items.body:
## Motivation

An edit service receives a fresh upload path for each request, even when several prompts reuse the same PNG. The default loader reopens and decompresses that reference during input validation. In a separate CPU profile of the measured fixture variants, Pillow took about 40 ms per large PNG. Hashing the compressed content and copying a previously decoded RGB image took about 3 ms.

## Modifications

The input-validation stage reuses decoded local RGB PNGs through the worker’s existing bounded conditioning cache. Each entry is keyed by a digest of the bytes passed to the decoder.

items.title: [Fix] cache: Respect row strides in convert_fp8
items.author: YuvrajSinghBhadoria2
items.summary: used as the number of elements to copy per row and advanced source and destination with the same flat index. For a column-sliced tensor such as, that copied the 32 padding columns and overwrote memory outside the logical destination slice.
items.body:
Fixes #70382.

`convert_fp8` used `src_cache.stride(0)` as the number of elements to copy per row and advanced source and destination with the same flat index. For a column-sliced tensor such as `base[:, :64]`, that copied the 32 padding columns and overwrote memory outside the logical destination slice.

This change:
- validates that source and destination have the same shape and contiguous inner dimensions,
- flattens contiguous trailing dimensions into `num_cols`,
- copies only `num_cols` elements per row using independent source/destination row strides, and
- returns early for empty inputs

## Motivation

A common A100/A800 PCIe server puts 4 GPUs behind two PCIe switches: GPUs 0–1 share one, GPUs 2–3 the other, and the switches meet at the CPU root complex, with no NVLink. On such a host:

items.summary: With, a request that waits on a secondary-to-CPU promotion can stay deferred indefinitely. Its chunks that are already in the CPU tier stay evictable while it waits, so other promotions and stores evict them, and its next lookup promotes them again.
items.body:
## Overview

With `TieringOffloadingSpec`, a request that waits on a secondary-to-CPU promotion can stay deferred indefinitely. Its chunks that are already in the CPU tier stay evictable while it waits, so other promotions and stores evict them, and its next lookup promotes them again. This PR holds those chunks until the request loads them or finishes.

Related: RFC #66782 (request-level promotions, pin until load).

items.title: [Bugfix][MoE] Use the real first local expert when EP does not divide num_experts
items.author: orangingq
items.summary: Fixes silent wrong expert weight computation in MoE EP kernels when ep_size doesn't evenly divide num_experts, by passing correct local_expert_offset to FusedMoE.
items.body:
## Purpose

When expert parallelism does not divide the number of experts, the TRT-LLM / FlashInfer MoE experts compute with the wrong expert weights on most ranks, silently.

`determine_expert_map` ("linear" placement) gives the first `num_experts % ep_size` ranks one extra expert. The TRT-LLM / FlashInfer experts, however, pass `local_expert_offset = ep_rank * num_local_experts` to the kernel, which assumes every rank holds the same number of experts. Example: 128 experts on EP7 → ranks 0–1 hold 19 experts, ranks 2–6 hold 18. Rank 2 owns experts 38–55, but the kernel is told its first expert

# What does this PR do?

Adds a second lookup backend for Engram tables that are row-sharded over DP x CP (`--engram-parallel-size`): a symmetric GIN/LSA device transport, ported from #7224. Inside an NVLink (LSA) domain a requester reads the owner's registered table rows directly; across domains, requests, rows and gradients travel over GPU-initiated networking (GIN). `--engram-communication-backend {symmetric,nccl}` selects the backend, and `symmetric` becomes the default for row groups of more than one rank.

items.author: haoyangli0109
items.summary: sgl-kernel's ROCm QuickReduce reduces bf16 in fp16 by default, and fp16 tops out at 65504. For the FP codec, guards that ceiling with a power-of-two prescale: it divides by S = 16 before the fp16 cast and multiplies back on output.
items.body:
## Motivation

sgl-kernel's ROCm QuickReduce reduces bf16 in fp16 by default (`ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_CAST_BF16_TO_FP16=1`), and fp16 tops out at 65504. For the FP codec, `main` guards that ceiling with a power-of-two prescale: it divides by S = 16 before the fp16 cast and multiplies back on output. That only moves fp16's window up by 16x, so both ends of the bf16 range still go wrong:

- Sums above 16 × 65504 (about 1.05e6) are clamped.
- Values below about 1e-4 fall into fp16's subnormal range after the division and lose mantissa bits; below about 5e-7 they become zero.

items.title: [Fix] multimodal: Load GLM-5.3-Flash media processors with a separate tokenizer
items.author: phphlio1
items.summary: With Transformers 5.19.0, GLM-5.3-Flash still loses its media processor when points to a tokenizer-only directory. SGLang asks to load from that directory, so the loader accepts a bare tokenizer even when contains valid image and video processor settings.
items.body:
## Motivation

With Transformers 5.19.0, GLM-5.3-Flash still loses its media processor when `--tokenizer-path` points to a tokenizer-only directory. SGLang asks `AutoProcessor` to load from that directory, so the loader accepts a bare tokenizer even when `--model-path` contains valid image and video processor settings.

Prevent filesystem offload write failures from aborting generation when block reuse flushes pending stores. This affects the built-in GDS backend added in #66805.

## Claims

- Wait for all requested I/O completions, including when an earlier completion fails.
- Preserve failed transfers for `get_finished()` to report through the existing connector cleanup path.
- Add regressions for failed-store reporting and waiting for remaining I/O.

## Validation

Base comparisons restore the parent's `wait()` with identical test and inference code.

## Overview

On `main` the specialized decode's DSA policy tables only have DCP16 entries, so TP8 x DCP8 decode workers (DSpark k = 4, 1-3 requests = 5-15 verify rows) fall back to the generic kernel forms, and the TP8 MoE / o_proj tables switch kernels at 17-40 rows in ways that make the step jump at the fourth and seventh request. items.title: [Bugfix][Model Loader] Layerwise reload: start over after a reload that raised
items.author: hallerite
items.summary: Fixes layerwise weight reload retry to discard buffered state from failed attempts, preventing stale/zeroed weights from being installed on recovery.
items.body:
## Overview

A layerwise weight reload that raises partway leaves layers on the meta device with their buffered weights, and the next `initialize_layerwise_reload` skips those layers as already initialized. A retried update then reports success while installing stale or zeroed weights. With this change, `initialize_layerwise_reload` first restores the live tensors of any layer an unfinished reload left behind and drops what that reload buffered, so the retry starts over. This complements #57854, which adds `abort_layerwise_reload` to the failure paths of vLLM's own weight-transfer engines.

This change reads the name with `getattr(loader, "__name__", None)` at both places that check it.

## Overview

**The problem.** Whisper runs its audio encoder more often than it needs to. With beam search, every beam step is a new engine request and re-encodes the same audio: 315 encoder runs for 5 requests (#49197). With language auto-detection (no `language` in the request), the first audio chunk is encoded twice: once to predict the language token and once to transcribe. That is the open follow-up item in #25750.

**How it works today.** Multimodal models keep encoder outputs in a bounded cache keyed by an item identifier. Encoder-decoder models bypass it: the scheduler always schedule

## Overview

A request that knows it will reuse a prefix can carry that prefix's block hashes in its KV-hint envelope (#53421 / #53423). Today that hint is only consumed by the request's own lookup, so the CPU-tier load starts when the request is scheduled - on its critical path. This PR lets the **offloading connector** act on the hint before any request exists: reserve GPU blocks by hash, load into them, publish them under those hashes, so the arriving prompt sees an ordinary prefix-cache hit. One new envelope action, no request/connector protocol change.

The dense FSDP training path divides the full logits tensor by temperature before computing token log-probabilities. With a large vocabulary, the extra buffer can take several GiB.

items.author: Autumn1998
items.summary: Adds AngularMuOwn optimizer support to MFSDP v2 in Megatron-LM, enabling per-row scale updates via Adam and Muon steps with Newton-Schulz decomposition.
items.body:
## Goal

Support the AngularMuOwn optimizer ([Muown Implicitly Performs Angular Step-size Decay](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.23637)) for Muon matrices under MFSDP v2, end to end in Megatron-LM: optimizer, MCore integration, and checkpoints.

## Background

AngularMuOwn writes each row as `W_i = g_i U_i`. Adam updates the signed row scales `g`; the unit directions `U` take a Muon step scaled by `lr * kappa_t` and are renormalized, with `kappa_t = (1 + c * max(0, t - t_w))^(-p)`. items.body:
## Problem

With `perf_metrics_output_dir` set, the disaggregated server should write one JSONL record for every request. For streaming requests, most records can be lost: clients disconnect as soon as they receive `data: [DONE]`, while the disaggregated record is appended only after the trailing performance-metrics event has been consumed. Under uvicorn's ASGI spec, Starlette cancels the streaming response on that disconnect before `on_resp_done` or the middleware's final-body path runs.

This supersedes #20280, rebasing the fix onto current main and addressing its remaining review findings.

items.body:
## Problem

`RolloutHealthMonitor.resume()` applies `--rollout-health-check-first-wait` (600 s by default) again after every resume. `generate` resumes the monitors at each rollout. A rollout that is shorter than the first wait therefore never gets a background check, and a hung engine is found only by the check at the end of the rollout. See the second half of #2551.

The wait after each resume protects engines that wake up (for example colocated engines after onload), so this change keeps it by default.

## Change

Add `--rollout-health-check-resume-wait` (float, default `None`).

items.title: Batch colocated expert weight updates across Megatron PP stages
items.author: leondada
items.summary: The rank-local expert update path from #2220 groups transfers by layer. When training pipeline stages are on different nodes, this can serialize the sending work across nodes even though the stages own independent weights.
items.body:
## Motivation

The rank-local expert update path from #2220 groups transfers by layer. When training pipeline stages are on different nodes, this can serialize the sending work across nodes even though the stages own independent weights. Each batch also incurs synchronization and a rollout-engine update.

On a colocated GLM-4.7 355B run (64 GPUs, training PP=8/EP=8), this patch reduces expert transfer batches from 89 to 12 at the same 10 GiB staging budget and cuts weight-update time from 38.5 s to 25.6 s per step (see Validation).

For LongRoPE checkpoints (128k Phi-3/Phi-3.5, Phi-4-mini) the PyTorch backend builds one RoPE table at load. items.title: [None][perf] Kimi K3.1: Helix Top-K merge writes the row mask and paged indices
items.author: zhaoyuanh-nvidia
items.summary: Under Helix CP, every DSA layer of a Kimi K3.1 generation server runs four small kernels on every rank after the key-sharded Top-K merge: -, which turns the kept token indices into the paged-pool indices the sparse attention reads; - three elementwise kernels …
items.body:
## Description

Follow-up to #22858. Under Helix CP, every DSA layer of a Kimi K3.1 generation server runs four small kernels on every rank after the key-sharded Top-K merge (`KeyShardTopKMerge.merge_owned`):

- `convert_req_index_to_global`, which turns the kept token indices into the paged-pool indices the sparse attention reads;
- three elementwise kernels in `MLA._attn_forward_gen` that build the mask of the rows the Helix combine must skip: the rows this rank holds no KV for (`helix_kv_bounds == 0`), the rows whose Top-K kept none of this rank's keys (kept count `== 0`), and their union.

items.title: [fsdp] fix: use actual chunk count for TiledMLP last-shard gradient write-back
items.author: four1er
items.summary: Fixes #8839 dropped parameter gradients accumulated by earlier micro-batches whenever returned fewer chunks than (e.g. moves any existing into its buffer and writes it back only from the hook installed with, and never fired in that case, so the accumulated gra…
items.body:
Fixes #8839

`TiledMLP.backward` dropped parameter gradients accumulated by earlier micro-batches whenever `torch.chunk` returned fewer chunks than `num_shards` (e.g. `n=9, shards=4` gives 3 chunks of 3). `GradientAccumulator` moves any existing `param.grad` into its buffer and writes it back only from the hook installed with `is_last_shard=True`, and `is_last_shard = i + 1 == shards` never fired in that case, so the accumulated gradients were silently lost.

This PR uses the actual chunk count (`len(x_shards)`) for the last-shard test, so the write-back hook always fires on the final shard.

### Feature request

For hybrid models (Qwen3.5, Qwen3-Next) on the SGLang rollout, hold each prompt's prefix state with an SGLang session (`--enable-session-radix-cache`, sglang >= 0.5.17, sgl-project/sglang#29173) until all samples of that prompt are done, then close the session.

### Motivation

A hybrid model can reuse a cached prefix only if the recurrent (Mamba) state at its end is still in SGLang's fixed-size state pool, which is evicted by LRU. With many prompts in flight, the prompts' states are the oldest and go first, so later samples of the same prompt recompute the whole prompt.

items.body:
Fixes #9713

## Bug

Rank 0 rewrote `latest_checkpointed_iteration.txt` with `open(..., 'w')` and `latest_train_state.pt` with `shutil.copy`, both in place, so a crash mid-save could leave an empty tracker behind. On restart `read_metadata` then printed `ERROR: Invalid metadata file ... Exiting` and called bare `sys.exit()`, exiting 0, so the job ended without training and a scheduler took it as success. With `--save-retain-interval` an empty tracker also failed every later save with a bare `int()` `ValueError`.

## Fix

- `megatron/training/checkpointing.py`: new `write_text_file_atomically()

items.body:
Continues #8915, which was closed automatically when its base branch was deleted after #9005 merged.

## What does this PR do?

## Summary

On the V1 FSDP path, `update_weights` (actor → rollout engine weight sync) broadcasts the **full parameter set every training step**. Measured cost on Qwen2.5-32B TP8: ~9 s/step, every step, regardless of how few parameters changed. Over hundreds of GRPO steps this is a fixed tax proportional to model size, not to actual weight drift.

## Suggestion

A bucketed delta mode would remove most of this cost:

- hash/checksum per parameter bucket, sync only buckets whose checksum changed (in practice almost none change every step in RL fine-tuning — the update is small relative to init)

### What does this PR do?

Fixes #8766.

In V1 trainers (`sync` and `colocate_async`), `_compute_advantage()` whitens advantages once over the full sampled batch, whereas `TrainingWorker.train_mini_batch()` splits the batch into `ppo_mini_batch_size` optimizer chunks without re-normalizing per chunk. This PR re-normalizes `mini_batch_td["advantages"]` per optimizer chunk in `TrainingWorker.train_mini_batch()`

items.author: GoldArowana
items.summary: GPQA accepts a letter-keyed object. The scorer reads its values in JSON insertion order and pairs them with by index.

GPQA accepts a letter-keyed `choices` object. The scorer reads its values in JSON insertion order and pairs them with `valid_letters` by index. Reordering the object can award a point for the wrong answer, even when `correct_letter` is set.

Align complete letter-keyed choice objects with the scorer's letter order before inferring a letter from label text or scoring a text response.

items.title: [algo, trainer, fsdp, megatron, cfg, doc] feat: add topk_rb KL loss (top-k Rao-Blackwellised KL to the reference)
items.author: hiddevandebeek
items.summary: It adds, a KL penalty against the reference policy for. The estimator computes KL(πθ ‖ πref) exactly over the reference top-k tokens plus one tail bucket.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Implements the RFC in #8536. It adds `actor.kl_loss_type: topk_rb`, a KL penalty against the reference policy for `use_kl_loss=True`.

The estimator computes KL(π_θ ‖ π_ref) exactly over the reference top-k tokens plus one tail bucket. The within-tail part is estimated from the sampled token, so the result is an **unbiased** estimate of the full-vocabulary KL gradient at every k, with much lower variance than the single-sample `kl`/`k2`/`low_var_kl`/`k3+` options. It is the per-token Rao-Blackwellised KL of [Amini et al., NeurIPS 2025](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.1063

## Summary

When context compaction splits an episode into multiple training rows, `rollout/raw_reward` gives that episode extra weight. For example, four episodes with rewards `[1, 0, 0, 0]` report a mean of `0.25`. Splitting the first and last episodes into two rows each raises the logged mean to `0.3333`, even though the episode rewards are identical.

Compute the mean over episodes before data-parallel partitioning. Each episode contributes equally, including when its segments land on different ranks. In the example above, the logged mean stays at `0.25` after splitting.

### What does this PR do?

Preserve vLLM's `finish_reason="length"` in `TokenOutput.stop_reason`. Today the vLLM rollout server reports `completed` both when generation stops naturally and when the output budget cuts it off. A caller translating this value to the Anthropic Messages API consequently sends `end_turn` for a truncated response, and the client can exit with work still in progress.

### Design and compatibility

Map vLLM's `stop` to `completed` and let `length` pass through the existing fallback. Callers can now return `max_tokens` to Anthropic clients. Abort still maps to `aborted`

items.author: R0k1e

## Motivation

`Float16Module.forward` upcasts the last pipeline stage's output to fp32 by default. slime calls the actor with `labels=None`, so the whole `[T, V]` logits tensor is copied to fp32. It is the largest single allocation in a long-context actor step: 40,960 tokens × 248,320 vocabulary is about 41 GB in fp32 versus 20 GB in bf16.

items.summary: This expression is nonnegative in real arithmetic, but subtracting 1 from a float32 exponential can erase the small KL term or make it negative when the policies are close. With valid finite log-probabilities near -0.1, I reproduced a value of -1.4901161e-8 wh…
items.body:
## Problem

For `k3` and `low_var_kl`, `compute_approx_kl` evaluates `exp(x) - 1 - x`, where `x = log_probs_base - log_probs`. This expression is nonnegative in real arithmetic, but subtracting 1 from a float32 exponential can erase the small KL term or make it negative when the policies are close.

With valid finite log-probabilities near -0.1, I reproduced a value of -1.4901161e-8 where an 80-digit reference gives 4.9986626e-11. The helper feeds the reported KL term and configured KL loss/reward paths; the Search-R1 example selects `low_var_kl` with a nonzero KL-loss coefficient.

items.body:
## Problem

With `--partial-rollout`, a sample aborted mid-generation goes back to the data buffer and is resumed later. `generate()` resumes it with a `max_new_tokens` budget reduced by `sample.response_length` and appends the new tokens after the existing response, so the request must be conditioned on that response.

For samples with images, the request is built as:

```python
payload["image_data"] = [...]
payload["text"] = sample.prompt
```

items.title: fix(data): give uniform reward groups exactly zero advantage
items.author: saloni-garg
items.summary: When every rollout in a prompt group gets the same fractional reward, there is no preference between them, so every advantage in the group should be exactly zero. In the group is centered in float32, and for identical rewards that can leave a residue of about …
items.body:
## What does this PR do?

When every rollout in a prompt group gets the same fractional reward, there is no preference between them, so every advantage in the group should be exactly zero. In `_post_process_rewards` the group is centered in float32, and for identical rewards that can leave a residue of about an ulp instead of zero. With std normalization on, the residue is then divided by its own std, which turns it into a small nonzero advantage shared by the whole group.

Small reproduction on current main (a group of 16 rollouts that all scored 0.3, `grpo` with `grpo_std_normalization`):

-
discussion: The nonzero advantages for uniform fractional rewards reproduce on `main`. I ran the grouped-reward tests at `0063710` on CPU with PyTorch 2.13.0: uniform groups produce exact zeros, and the mixed-group and nonfinite-reward cases pass too.
Thank you for checking, and for reproducing it on main as well. Glad the tests hold up on your side too. Happy to run anything else you would like to see here.

`grade_answer_verl` (`slime/rollout/rm_hub/math_utils.py:485`) starts with:

## Background

Multi-model SGLang configuration was resolved incrementally while deployment side effects were already being prepared. Invalid topology or ambiguous model entries could therefore fail late, after router or placement setup had begun.

## Problem

The config path did not validate whole-file invariants such as duplicate model names, multiple weight-updated models, complete engine topology, PP/TP consistency, or multi-node divisibility before launch.

## Solution

- Resolve every model and validate the complete config before placement or router startup.
- Reject unknown model fields

## Background

Locally managed SGLang servers are polled through `/health_generate` before rollout initialization can continue.

## Problem

The startup poll had neither a request timeout nor an overall deadline. A hung health request could block startup indefinitely, and failures while waiting left the newly spawned server process tree running.

## Solution

- Add `--sglang-server-startup-timeout` with a positive finite value and a conservative 600-second default.
- Use a monotonic deadline and cap every health request by both five seconds and the remaining startup budget.
- Reject readiness

## Background

`generate_and_rm_group` supports custom generation that fans one input out into `list[Sample]`, so a fully-async task can return `list[list[Sample]]`.

## Problem

The done callback inspected only the outer list. An aborted leaf inside a fan-out result could therefore enter the completed queue. Requeuing that nested output directly is also invalid because the next generation expects a flat input group.

## Solution

- Snapshot the flat input group before generation can mutate it.
- Inspect one-level fan-out leaves for `Sample.Status.ABORTED`.
- Requeue the pristine flat snapshot

## Problem

`MegatronTrainRayActor.init()` backs up the actor and then loads reference, teacher, or old-actor checkpoints into the same model.

Without `--offload-train`, initialization leaves the last auxiliary checkpoint active. Both training entry points synchronize rollout weights before the first training step, so distributed or disk-based synchronization can publish auxiliary weights instead of the resumed actor.

For one resumed run:

| | rollout logprob | reference logprob | actor logprob |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Before | -0.1106 | -0.1111 | -0.1471 |
| After | -0.1088 | -0.1421 | -0.1

## Summary

Fix CUDA autocast from downcasting the FP32 reduction used by VIME's fused PPO entropy path.

Under CUDA autocast, `torch.einsum` can run at a reduced precision even when both operands were explicitly promoted to FP32. The result is saved for entropy backward, so the precision loss affects both the reported entropy value and its gradient.

This change keeps only that CUDA reduction outside autocast and adds a one-GPU regression suite covering FP16/BF16 autocast, masked/unmasked log-prob paths, metric-only/gradient entropy, and chunked/non-chunked execution.

items.author: yuyz-cyber

items.body:
## Problem

Training and evaluation launch rollout tasks concurrently at three levels: samples within a rollout group, rollout groups within a training batch, and samples within an evaluation batch.

When one task raises an exception, the exception is propagated but the unfinished sibling tasks are not cancelled. They can continue generation or reward computation after the rollout has failed, wasting resources and potentially leaving unobserved task exceptions in the event loop.

## Fix

At each concurrency boundary, cancel unfinished sibling tasks and wait for their cleanup before re-raising

Enabling KL (--kl-coef 0.1 or --use-kl-loss) without --ref-load used to die in slime_validate_args with `TypeError: _path_exists: path should be string, bytes, os.PathLike or integer, not NoneType`, because it stat'd args.ref_load before checking it was set. This adds the same guard: ref_load unset now raises a ValueError telling the user to pass --ref-load, and a ref_load that points nowhere still raises the original FileNotFoundError. Two unit tests cover both cases.

`_parse_extra_env_vars` split each assignment on every `=` and then kept only the second component. For example:

items.title: [CI/Build] Run the CPU tests CI silently skips, and guard against new gaps
items.author: natedemoss
items.summary: goes into synchronized upstream CPU tests, which runs in — it imports, so it needs vLLM present. It fails when a test file is neither referenced by a CI job nor waived in, and when a file CI runs as bare has no entry point.
items.body:
## Problem

CI enumerates test files by hand — one `python tests/<file>.py` line per test in `.buildkite/pipeline.yml`, one `(file, num_gpus, ...)` tuple in `.buildkite/gpu_suites.py`. Nothing walks `tests/`, so a test only runs if its author also wired it into a job. Two failure modes, both of which leave CI green:

1. **The file is never wired in.** Three existing files are in this state today and have never run in CI:
   - `tests/test_qwen3_linear_attention_cu_seqlens.py`
   - `tests/test_chunked_gae.py`
   - `tests/test_rollout_metrics.py`

2. **The CPU job's invocation style fails open.**

items.title: Order pipeline weight-update process groups across rollout engines
items.author: chengcuiping
items.summary: The PP sources are Ray actors invoked concurrently. Each rollout-engine actor uses a blocking HTTP call to join a group and processes methods serially. [Discussion: @zhuzilin, could you please take a look at this PR when you have time?]
items.body:
## Problem

In non-colocated full NCCL weight updates with pipeline-parallel training and multiple independent SGLang rollout engines, each PP source creates a custom `slime-pp_<rank>` group containing itself and every engine GPU.

The PP sources are Ray actors invoked concurrently. Each rollout-engine actor uses a blocking HTTP call to join a group and processes methods serially. If engine 0 starts PP0 while engine 1 starts PP1, each group waits for the request queued behind the other engine's blocking call. The existing rollout-engine lock only covers later broadcasts, so it cannot prevent t
discussion:
@zhuzilin, could you please take a look at this PR when you have time?

It fixes a reproducible deadlock in non-colocated pipeline-parallel weight updates with multiple rollout engines by ordering the process-group connect and disconnect
